oracle_provenance: Glasberg & Moore (1990) ERB auditory-filter model, independently hand-verified before implementation against the commonly cited ~132 Hz ERB figure at 1 kHz; not copied from any shared Skill fixture.
scope: Bounded auditory-filter (critical) bandwidth prediction checked against a declared claim; not a listener preference, discomfort or annoyance judgment.

cases.question: Does a claimed critical bandwidth matching the ERB model at 1 kHz pass within tight tolerance?
Below the model's documented 100 Hz-10 kHz fitted range, is the result flagged as outside applicability rather than silently trusted?
Must a non-positive center frequency be rejected rather than silently used?
When a claimed bandwidth deviates well beyond tolerance from the ERB prediction, is that flagged rather than silently accepted as a real listener effect?
